title: Prakrama 3, Sarga 8. Beholding Mahadeva
html:
The Lord comes to Ekamraka (Bhubaneshvara), the city of Shiva that rivals Kashi; the temple, the city and the Bindu-sarovara pond are described; bowing to Krittivasa, He offers Shiva a hymn of eight verses, praying for love of Hari

Verse 1

ततः प्रयातो द्विजराजविक्रमः
क्रमेण यत्राखिललोकपालैः।
एकाम्रकाख्ये गिरिजासमन्वितो
गिरीशदेवो गिरिराजमूर्धनि॥१॥

tataḥ prayāto dvijarājavikramaḥ
krameṇa yatrākhilalokapālaiḥ|
ekāmrakākhye girijāsamanvito
girīśadevo girirājamūrdhani||1||

tatah — then; prayatah — having set out; dvija-raja-vikramah — striding like the king of birds; kramena — by stages; yatra — where; akhila-loka-palaih — with all the guardians of the worlds; ekamraka-akhye — in the place called Ekamraka; girija-samanvitah — together with Girija; girisha-devah — the god Girisha; giri-raja-murdhani — on the summit of the king of mountains.

1Then, striding like the king of birds, He came by stages to the place called Ekamraka1, where on the summit of the king of mountains the god Girisha dwells with Girija and all the guardians of the worlds.

Verse 2

ददर्श तत्राखिलशोभयोज्ज्वलं
चलत्पताकं शिवमन्दिरं महत्।
सुधावलिप्तं वरशृङ्गमुन्नतं
सुतोरणं श्वेतगिरिमिवापरम्॥२॥

dadarśa tatrākhilaśobhayojjvalaṁ
calatpatākaṁ śivamandiraṁ mahat|
sudhāvaliptaṁ varaśṛṅgamunnataṁ
sutoraṇaṁ śvetagirimivāparam||2||

dadarsha — He saw; tatra — there; akhila-shobhaya — with every beauty; ujjvalam — shining; chalat-patakam — with fluttering banners; shiva-mandiram — the temple of Shiva; mahat — great; sudha-avaliptam — whitewashed; vara-shringam — with a splendid spire; unnatam — lofty; su-toranam — with fine gateways; shveta-girim — the White Mountain; iva — like; aparam — a second.

2There He saw the great temple of Shiva, shining with every beauty, its banners fluttering, whitewashed and lofty, with a splendid spire and fine gateways — like a second White Mountain2.

Verse 3

निपत्य भूमौ प्रणनाम देवः
शिवालयं शूलविचित्रचूडम्।
पताकया नाकनदीविभङ्गं
दधत्समारोहति हेलयेव॥३॥

nipatya bhūmau praṇanāma devaḥ
śivālayaṁ śūlavicitracūḍam|
patākayā nākanadīvibhaṅgaṁ
dadhatsamārohati helayeva||3||

nipatya — falling; bhumau — to the ground; prananama — bowed; devah — the Lord; shiva-alayam — to the abode of Shiva; shula-vichitra-chudam — its pinnacle adorned with a trident; patakaya — with its banner; naka-nadi-vibhangam — the wave of the heavenly river; dadhat — bearing; samarohati — rises up; helaya — playfully; iva — as if.

3Falling to the ground, the Lord bowed to that abode of Shiva crowned with a trident: bearing on its banner a wave of the heavenly river, it seems to rise playfully into the sky.

Verse 4

ततो जगामेश्वरदर्शनाय
पुरीं पुरारेः परया मुदा सः।
वसन्ति यत्रेश्वरलिङ्गकोट्यो
विश्वेश्वराद्याश्च सुपुण्यतीर्थाः॥४॥

tato jagāmeśvaradarśanāya
purīṁ purāreḥ parayā mudā saḥ|
vasanti yatreśvaraliṅgakoṭyo
viśveśvarādyāśca supuṇyatīrthāḥ||4||

tatah — then; jagama — went; ishvara-darshanaya — to see the lord (Shiva); purim — to the city; purareh — of Purari; paraya — supreme; muda — with joy; sah — He; vasanti — dwell; yatra — where; ishvara-linga-kotyah — millions of lingas of the lord; vishveshvara-adyah — headed by Vishveshvara; cha — and; su-punya-tirthah — most holy tirthas.

4Then with supreme joy He went into the city of Purari3 to behold its lord. There dwell millions of that lord's lingas, headed by Vishveshvara, and most holy tirthas.

Verse 5

प्रासादकोट्यो वरतोरणाढ्या
राजन्ति राजच्चलचेलचूडाः।
आमुक्तभूषा मनुजा मनोज्ञ-
गन्धार्चिता इन्द्रपदापितेहाः॥५॥

prāsādakoṭyo varatoraṇāḍhyā
rājanti rājaccalacelacūḍāḥ|
āmuktabhūṣā manujā manojña-
gandhārcitā indrapadāpitehāḥ||5||

prasada-kotyah — millions of mansions; vara-torana-adhyah — rich in fine gateways; rajanti — shine; rajat-chala-chela-chudah — their tops hung with gleaming, fluttering cloth; amukta-bhushah — wearing ornaments; manujah — men; manojna-gandha-architah — anointed with lovely perfumes; indra-pada-apita-ihah — their desires fulfilled as in the realm of Indra.

5There millions of mansions shine, rich in fine gateways, their tops hung with gleaming, fluttering cloth; and the people, decked with ornaments and anointed with lovely perfumes, have all they desire, as in the realm of Indra4.

Verse 6

तीर्थानि कोट्यो मणिकर्णिकाद्या
वसन्ति यत्राशु विमुक्तदेहाः।
गच्छन्ति निःश्रेयसमुग्रयोगै-
र्यं योगिनो यान्ति चतुर्युगेन॥६॥

tīrthāni koṭyo maṇikarṇikādyā
vasanti yatrāśu vimuktadehāḥ|
gacchanti niḥśreyasamugrayogai-
ryaṁ yogino yānti caturyugena||6||

tirthani — tirthas; kotyah — millions; manikarnika-adyah — headed by Manikarnika; vasanti — are; yatra — where; ashu — at once; vimukta-dehah — those who have left the body; gachchhanti — attain; nihshreyasam — the highest good (liberation); ugra-yogaih — by fierce yoga; yam — which; yoginah — yogis; yanti — reach; chatur-yugena — in four yugas.

6There are millions of tirthas headed by Manikarnika5; whoever leaves the body there at once attains liberation, which yogis reach through fierce yoga over four ages.

Verse 7

बिन्दून्समाहृत्य समस्ततीर्थात्
कृतं महाबिन्दुसरोवराख्यम्।
कुण्डं कृतं देववरेण यत्र
स्नानाल्लभेच्चैव पदं विशुद्धम्॥७॥

bindūnsamāhṛtya samastatīrthāt
kṛtaṁ mahābindusarovarākhyam|
kuṇḍaṁ kṛtaṁ devavareṇa yatra
snānāllabheccaiva padaṁ viśuddham||7||

bindun — drops; samahritya — gathering; samasta-tirthat — from all the tirthas; kritam — made; maha-bindu-sarovara-akhyam — called Maha-Bindu-sarovara; kundam — a pond; kritam — was made; deva-varena — by the best of the gods; yatra — where; snanat — by bathing; labhet — one will gain; cha — and; eva — indeed; padam — the abode; vishuddham — pure.

7There the best of the gods gathered drops from all the tirthas and made a pond called Maha-Bindu-sarovara6; by bathing in it one attains the pure abode.

Verse 8

काशीं विहायाशु विशुद्धविक्रमो
वासाय यत्राखिलतीर्थपुण्यान्।
आहूय तत्क्षेत्रवरे वरेण्यः
संस्थापयामास महेशदेवः॥८॥

kāśīṁ vihāyāśu viśuddhavikramo
vāsāya yatrākhilatīrthapuṇyān|
āhūya tatkṣetravare vareṇyaḥ
saṁsthāpayāmāsa maheśadevaḥ||8||

kashim — Kashi; vihaya — leaving; ashu — swiftly; vishuddha-vikramah — pure in his might; vasaya — to dwell; yatra — where; akhila-tirtha-punyan — all the holy tirthas; ahuya — summoning; tat-kshetra-vare — in that best of sacred lands; varenyah — the most worthy; samsthapayam asa — established; mahesha-devah — the god Mahesha.

8Swiftly leaving Kashi to dwell here, the most worthy god Mahesha, pure in his might, summoned all the holy tirthas and established them in this best of sacred lands.

Verse 9

स कृत्तिवासाः स्वयमेव देवः
स लिङ्गरूपी वसतीश्वरी च।
भुङ्क्ते स्वयं भोगवरानशेषा-
न्दिव्यान्यतीन्द्रैरभिवन्द्यमानः॥९॥

sa kṛttivāsāḥ svayameva devaḥ
sa liṅgarūpī vasatīśvarī ca|
bhuṅkte svayaṁ bhogavarānaśeṣā-
ndivyānyatīndrairabhivandyamānaḥ||9||

sah — he; krittivasah — Krittivasa; svayam — himself; eva — indeed; devah — the god; sah — he; linga-rupi — in the form of a linga; vasati — dwells; ishvari — Ishvari; cha — and; bhunkte — enjoys; svayam — himself; bhoga-varan — the finest delights; asheshan — all; divyan — divine; yati-indraih — by the lords of ascetics; abhivandyamanah — being worshipped.

9The god Krittivasa7 himself dwells here in the form of a linga, and Ishvari with him; worshipped by the lords of ascetics, he himself enjoys every exquisite divine delight.

Verse 10

सुगन्धमाल्यैर्वरचन्द्रवर्ति-
दीपावलीभिः समलङ्कृताङ्गम्।
मृदङ्गघोषैर्वरशङ्खनादै-
र्देवीभिरानृत्यपराभिराढ्यम्॥१०॥

sugandhamālyairvaracandravarti-
dīpāvalībhiḥ samalaṅkṛtāṅgam|
mṛdaṅgaghoṣairvaraśaṅkhanādai-
rdevībhirānṛtyaparābhirāḍhyam||10||

su-gandha-malyaih — with fragrant garlands; vara-chandra-varti-dipa-avalibhih — with rows of lamps with wicks of fine camphor; samalankrita-angam — adorned in every part; mridanga-ghoshaih — with the boom of mridangas; vara-shankha-nadaih — with the call of fine conches; devibhih — with goddesses (dancing women); anritya-parabhih — absorbed in dance; adhyam — rich.

10Adorned with fragrant garlands and rows of lamps with wicks of fine camphor, filled with the boom of mridangas, the call of fine conches, and goddesses absorbed in dance8 —

Verse 11

विवेश भृत्यैर्भवनं पुरारेः
सुधांशुगौरस्य हरिः परेशः।
यथा महेन्द्रस्य महोत्सवाढ्यं
पद्मोद्भवः कृष्णपदाब्जभृङ्गः॥११॥

viveśa bhṛtyairbhavanaṁ purāreḥ
sudhāṁśugaurasya hariḥ pareśaḥ|
yathā mahendrasya mahotsavāḍhyaṁ
padmodbhavaḥ kṛṣṇapadābjabhṛṅgaḥ||11||

vivesha — entered; bhrityaih — with His servants; bhavanam — the house; purareh — of Purari; sudhamshu-gaurasya — white as the moon; harih — Hari; para-ishah — the supreme Lord; yatha — as; mahendrasya — of the great Indra; maha-utsava-adhyam — rich in great festivals; padma-udbhavah — the Lotus-born; krishna-pada-abja-bhringah — a bee at the lotus feet of Krishna.

11such was the house of Purari, white as the moon, which Hari, the supreme Lord, entered with His servants, as the Lotus-born9, a bee at the lotus feet of Krishna, enters the festive palace of the great Indra.

Verse 12

स कृत्तिवासं शिरसा ववन्द
निवास्य देहं भुवि दण्डवत्स्वम्।
गिरा गिरीशं च सगद्गदेन
तुष्टाव संहृष्टतनू रथाङ्गी॥१२॥

sa kṛttivāsaṁ śirasā vavanda
nivāsya dehaṁ bhuvi daṇḍavatsvam|
girā girīśaṁ ca sagadgadena
tuṣṭāva saṁhṛṣṭatanū rathāṅgī||12||

sah — He; krittivasam — to Krittivasa; shirasa — with His head; vavanda — bowed; nivasya — laying; deham — body; bhuvi — on the ground; dandavat — like a staff; svam — His own; gira — with speech; girisham — Girisha; cha — and; sa-gadgadena — faltering; tushtava — praised; samhrishta-tanuh — His body thrilling with rapture; rathangi — the Bearer of the discus.

12Laying His body on the ground like a staff, He bowed His head before Krittivasa; and the Bearer of the discus, His body thrilling with rapture, praised Girisha in a faltering voice10:

Verse 13

नमो नमस्ते त्रिदशेश्वराय
भूतादिनाथाय मृडाय नित्यम्।
गङ्गातरङ्गोत्थितबालचन्द्र-
चूडाय गौरीनयनोत्सवाय॥१३॥

namo namaste tridaśeśvarāya
bhūtādināthāya mṛḍāya nityam|
gaṅgātaraṅgotthitabālacandra-
cūḍāya gaurīnayanotsavāya||13||

namah — obeisance; namah — obeisance; te — to you; tridasha-ishvaraya — the lord of the Thirty; bhuta-adi-nathaya — the master of the bhutas and other beings; mridaya — to Mrida (the Gracious); nityam — ever; ganga-taranga-utthita-bala-chandra-chudaya — whose crest is the young moon rising from the waves of the Ganga; gauri-nayana-utsavaya — the festival of Gauri's eyes.

13"Obeisance, obeisance to you for ever — lord of the Thirty, master of the bhutas and all other beings, Mrida the Gracious, whose crest is the young moon rising from the waves of the Ganga, festival of Gauri's eyes!

Verse 14

सुतप्तचामीकरचन्द्रनील-
पद्मप्रवालाम्बुदकान्तिवक्त्रैः।
सुनृत्यरङ्गेष्टवरप्रदाय
कैवल्यनाथाय वृषध्वजाय॥१४॥

sutaptacāmīkaracandranīla-
padmapravālāmbudakāntivaktraiḥ|
sunṛtyaraṅgeṣṭavarapradāya
kaivalyanāthāya vṛṣadhvajāya||14||

su-tapta-chamikara-chandra-nila-padma-pravala-ambuda-kanti-vaktraih — with faces shining like molten gold, the moon, the blue lotus, coral and the rain-cloud; su-nritya-range — in the arena of splendid dance; ishta-vara-pradaya — who grants the boons desired; kaivalya-nathaya — to the lord of kaivalya; vrisha-dhvajaya — whose emblem is the bull.

14Obeisance to him whose faces shine like molten gold, the moon, the blue lotus, coral and the rain-cloud11, who in the arena of his splendid dance grants the boons desired — to the lord of kaivalya, whose emblem is the bull!

Verse 15

सुधांशुसूर्याग्निविलोचनेन
तमोभिदे ते जगतः शिवाय।
सहस्रशुभ्रांशुसहस्ररश्मि-
सहस्रसंजित्वरतेजसेऽस्तु॥१५॥

sudhāṁśusūryāgnivilocanena
tamobhide te jagataḥ śivāya|
sahasraśubhrāṁśusahasraraśmi-
sahasrasaṁjitvaratejase'stu||15||

sudhamshu-surya-agni-vilochanena — with eyes that are moon, sun and fire; tamah-bhide — who dispels darkness; te — to you; jagatah — of the world; shivaya — to the good; sahasra-shubhramshu-sahasra-rashmi-sahasra-samjitvara-tejase — whose splendour outshines thousands of moons and thousands of suns; astu — be (obeisance).

15Obeisance be to you, who with your eyes — the moon, the sun and fire — dispel the darkness; to you, the good of the world, whose splendour outshines thousands of moons and thousands of suns!

Verse 16

नागेशरत्नोज्ज्वलविग्रहाय
शार्दूलचर्मांशुकदिव्यतेजसे।
सहस्रपत्रोपरि संस्थिताय
वराङ्गदामुक्तभुजद्वयाय॥१६॥

nāgeśaratnojjvalavigrahāya
śārdūlacarmāṁśukadivyatejase|
sahasrapatropari saṁsthitāya
varāṅgadāmuktabhujadvayāya||16||

naga-isha-ratna-ujjvala-vigrahaya — whose form blazes with the jewels of the king of serpents; shardula-charma-amshuka-divya-tejase — divinely radiant in a garment of tiger-skin; sahasra-patra-upari — upon a thousand-petalled lotus; samsthitaya — seated; vara-angada-amukta-bhuja-dvayaya — whose two arms wear splendid armlets.

16Obeisance to him whose form blazes with the jewels of the king of serpents, who is divinely radiant in a garment of tiger-skin, who is seated on a thousand-petalled lotus, whose two arms wear splendid armlets;

Verse 17

सुनूपुरारञ्जितपादपद्म-
क्षरत्सुधाभृत्यसुखप्रदाय।
विचित्ररत्नौघविभूषिताय
प्रेमाणमेवाद्य हरौ विधेहि॥१७॥

sunūpurārañjitapādapadma-
kṣaratsudhābhṛtyasukhapradāya|
vicitraratnaughavibhūṣitāya
premāṇamevādya harau vidhehi||17||

su-nupura-aranjita-pada-padma-ksharat-sudha-bhritya-sukha-pradaya — who gives joy to his servants with the nectar flowing from his lotus feet graced with fine anklets; vichitra-ratna-augha-vibhushitaya — adorned with a host of wondrous jewels; premanam — love; eva — indeed; adya — today; harau — for Hari; vidhehi — grant.

17to him who gives joy to his servants with the nectar flowing from his lotus feet graced with fine anklets; to him who is adorned with a host of wondrous jewels! Grant now love — love for Hari!

Verse 18

श्रीराम गोविन्द मुकुन्द शौरे
श्रीकृष्ण नारायण वासुदेव।
इत्यादिनामामृतपानमत्त-
भृङ्गाधिपायाखिलदुःखहन्त्रे॥१८॥

śrīrāma govinda mukunda śaure
śrīkṛṣṇa nārāyaṇa vāsudeva|
ityādināmāmṛtapānamatta-
bhṛṅgādhipāyākhiladuḥkhahantre||18||

shri-rama — O Sri Rama; govinda — O Govinda; mukunda — O Mukunda; shaure — O Shauri; shri-krishna — O Sri Krishna; narayana — O Narayana; vasudeva — O Vasudeva; iti-adi-nama-amrita-pana-matta-bhringa-adhipaya — to the king of the bees drunk on the nectar of such names; akhila-duhkha-hantre — the destroyer of all sorrow.

18To him who is the king of the bees drunk on the nectar of names such as 'Sri Rama, Govinda, Mukunda, Shauri, Sri Krishna, Narayana, Vasudeva', to the destroyer of all sorrow — obeisance!

Verse 19

श्रीनारदाद्यैः सततं सुगोप्य-
जिज्ञासितायाशु वरप्रदाय।
तेभ्यो हरेर्भक्तिसुखप्रदाय
शिवाय सर्वगुरवे नमो नमः॥१९॥

śrīnāradādyaiḥ satataṁ sugopya-
jijñāsitāyāśu varapradāya|
tebhyo harerbhaktisukhapradāya
śivāya sarvagurave namo namaḥ||19||

shri-narada-adyaih — by Sri Narada and others; satatam — constantly; su-gopya-jijnasitaya — who is asked about what is most secret; ashu — swiftly; vara-pradaya — who grants boons; tebhyah — to them; hareh — for Hari; bhakti-sukha-pradaya — who grants the joy of devotion; shivaya — to Shiva; sarva-gurave — the guru of all; namah — obeisance; namah — obeisance.

19To him whom Sri Narada and others constantly ask about what is most secret, who swiftly grants boons, who grants them the joy of devotion to Hari — to Shiva, the guru of all, obeisance, obeisance!

Verse 20

श्रीगौरीनेत्रोत्सवमङ्गलाय
तत्प्राणनाथाय रसप्रदाय।
सदा समुत्कण्ठगोविन्दलीला-
गानप्रवीणाय नमोऽस्तु तुभ्यम्॥२०॥

śrīgaurīnetrotsavamaṅgalāya
tatprāṇanāthāya rasapradāya|
sadā samutkaṇṭhagovindalīlā-
gānapravīṇāya namo'stu tubhyam||20||

shri-gauri-netra-utsava-mangalaya — the auspicious festival of Sri Gauri's eyes; tat-prana-nathaya — the lord of her life; rasa-pradaya — the giver of rasa; sada — ever; samutkantha-govinda-lila-gana-pravinaya — skilled in singing with longing the lilas of Govinda; namah — obeisance; astu — be; tubhyam — to you.

20To you, the auspicious festival of Sri Gauri's eyes, the lord of her life, the giver of rasa, ever skilled in singing with longing of the lilas of Govinda — obeisance to you!"

Verse 21

एतच्छिवस्याष्टकमद्भुतं महत्
शृण्वन्हरिप्रेम लभेत शीघ्रम्।
ज्ञानं च विज्ञानमपूर्ववैभवं
यो भावपूर्णः परमं समादरम्॥२१॥

etacchivasyāṣṭakamadbhutaṁ mahat
śṛṇvanhariprema labheta śīghram|
jñānaṁ ca vijñānamapūrvavaibhavaṁ
yo bhāvapūrṇaḥ paramaṁ samādaram||21||

etat — this; shivasya — of Shiva; ashtakam — octad; adbhutam — wonderful; mahat — great; shrinvan — hearing; hari-prema — love for Hari; labheta — will gain; shighram — soon; jnanam — knowledge; cha — and; vijnanam — realization; apurva-vaibhavam — unprecedented glory; yah — who; bhava-purnah — full of feeling; paramam — the highest; samadaram — honour.

21Whoever, full of feeling, hears this wonderful and great octad to Shiva will soon gain love for Hari, knowledge and realization, unprecedented glory and the highest honour.

Verse 22

इति स्तुवन्तं […]मुत्सुकाः
शिवस्य भृत्या वरमाल्यगन्धैः।
विभूषयामासुरनुत्तमाङ्गं
ततो बहिर्वेश्मसु संनिविष्टः॥२२॥

iti stuvantaṁ […]mutsukāḥ
śivasya bhṛtyā varamālyagandhaiḥ|
vibhūṣayāmāsuranuttamāṅgaṁ
tato bahirveśmasu saṁniviṣṭaḥ||22||

iti — thus; stuvantam — Him who was praising; […] — (lacuna); utsukah — eager; shivasya — of Shiva; bhrityah — the servants; vara-malya-gandhaih — with fine garlands and perfumes; vibhushayam asuh — adorned; anuttama-angam — Him of incomparable form; tatah — then; bahih — outside; veshmasu — in houses; samnivishtah — He settled.

22The servants of Shiva eagerly adorned Him who had thus praised […]12, Him of incomparable form, with fine garlands and perfumes; then He settled in houses outside the temple.

Verse 23

भक्तार्पितान्नं बुभुजे ततोऽसौ
सुप्त्वा मुदा तत्र निशां निनाय।
प्रातः समुत्थाय स कृष्णलीलां
गायन्सुखेनापि बभूव पूर्णः॥२३॥

bhaktārpitānnaṁ bubhuje tato'sau
suptvā mudā tatra niśāṁ nināya|
prātaḥ samutthāya sa kṛṣṇalīlāṁ
gāyansukhenāpi babhūva pūrṇaḥ||23||

bhakta-arpita-annam — food offered by the devotees; bubhuje — ate; tatah — then; asau — He; suptva — sleeping; muda — joyfully; tatra — there; nisham — the night; ninaya — spent; pratah — in the morning; samutthaya — rising; sah — He; krishna-lilam — the lila of Krishna; gayan — singing; sukhena — with happiness; api — too; babhuva — became; purnah — filled.

23Then He ate the food offered by the devotees and spent the night there in happy sleep; and in the morning He rose, sang the lila of Krishna, and was filled with happiness.

Verse 24

पठेद्य इत्थं स्तवमम्बुजाक्ष-
कृतं पुरारेः पुरुषोत्तमस्य।
प्रेमाणमेवात्र लभेत नित्यं
सुदुर्लभं यन्मुनिदेववृन्दैः॥२४॥

paṭhedya itthaṁ stavamambujākṣa-
kṛtaṁ purāreḥ puruṣottamasya|
premāṇamevātra labheta nityaṁ
sudurlabhaṁ yanmunidevavṛndaiḥ||24||

pathet — recites; yah — who; ittham — thus; stavam — the hymn; ambuja-aksha-kritam — composed by the Lotus-eyed; purareh — to Purari; purushottamasya — by Purushottama; premanam — love; eva — indeed; atra — here (in this life); labheta — will gain; nityam — eternal; su-durlabham — very hard to attain; yat — which; muni-deva-vrindaih — for the hosts of sages and gods.

24Whoever recites this hymn to Purari, composed by the lotus-eyed Purushottama13, will gain even here eternal love, so hard to attain even for the hosts of sages and gods.

Thus ends the eighth sarga, "Beholding Mahadeva" (Mahadeva-darshana), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Ekamraka (Ekamra) is Bhubaneshvara in Orissa, the holy city of Shiva. Girisha ("Lord of the Mountains") and Girija ("Daughter of the Mountains") are Shiva and Parvati; the "king of mountains" is the Himalaya, where Shiva dwells on Kailasa: here in Ekamraka he dwells just as he does there.
  2. The White Mountain is Kailasa, the abode of Shiva.
  3. Purari ("Enemy of the Three Cities") is Shiva, who burned the three flying cities of the asuras.
  4. The reading and sense of this passage are uncertain.
  5. Manikarnika is a famous tirtha (ghat) in Kashi; the description of Ekamraka echoes Kashi, since Shiva brought the holy places of Kashi here (v. 8). Vishveshvara is the principal linga of Kashi.
  6. Bindu-sarovara ("the Lake of Drops") is a sacred pond in Bhubaneshvara.
  7. Krittivasa ("Clad in a Hide") is Shiva; this is the name of the principal linga of Bhubaneshvara (the Lingaraja temple). Ishvari is his consort.
  8. Apparently the temple dancers.
  9. Brahma, who was born from the lotus growing from Vishnu's navel.
  10. The Lord, playing the part of a devotee, honours Shiva as the greatest of Vaishnavas (cf. Bhagavata Purana 12.13.16: "as Shambhu among the Vaishnavas") and asks of him only love for Hari (vv. 17–20). This neither places Shiva above the Lord nor makes them equal: Shiva himself is drunk on the names of Hari and sings of Govinda's lilas (vv. 18, 20), and Brahma is "a bee at the lotus feet of Krishna" (v. 11).
  11. Understood as the five faces of Shiva, each of its own colour. The reading is conjectural.
  12. All the editions have a lacuna of a few syllables here (probably a name or epithet of the Lord).
  13. That is, by the Lord Himself; it may also be understood as "will gain love for Purushottama".
